answers.q1: Mira alphabetizes the spice shelf without thinking, remembers the tiny details people mention once, and can tell when someone at a table has not found their way into the conversation yet. On road trips she builds a hand-written playlist before anyone asks.
answers.q2: My favorite memory is a rainy Saturday at the Harbor Street book market. The lights flickered, so we carried our paper bags to the window seat at Dot Cafe, split a cinnamon roll, and watched the rain clear. Mira folded the empty receipt into tiny boats while we waited.
answers.q3: I admire that Mira makes room for people in practical ways: she asks the quieter person a real question, remembers the answer, and calls when she says she will. Her kindness is steady enough that people can lean on it.
answers.q4: After the receipt boats at Dot Cafe, we started calling ourselves the tiny boat committee. At Saturday pancakes, the first pancake is always the cook's, even if it comes out lopsided. Those two rules can rescue almost any ordinary morning.
answers.q5: Right now Mira goes to ceramics at Farrow Studio every Wednesday, tends tomato pots on the kitchen-window sill, and keeps adding songs to the playlist she takes on Sunday walks. She likes the North Loop farmers market for the flowers and the slow start to the weekend.
answers.q6: For this birthday I want Mira to hear that the care she gives everyone else deserves to find its way back to her. I hope 25 brings slow mornings, music for every walk, clay under her fingernails, and plenty of room around the table. I am proud to be her sister, and I love the life we keep making in small pieces.
